rule: Build PR bodies from the checked-in .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md rather than a hardcoded copy, and preserve the template's instructional HTML comments and mandated section text instead of stripping all comments.
trigger: Agent instructions, tooling, or docs that generate a PR body embed their own copy of the template, or instruct that all HTML comments be removed from the template.
rationale: The template carries required constraints ("Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template!") and per-section guidance; hardcoding it drifts from upstream and blanket comment-stripping drops obligations reviewers rely on.

evidence.excerpt: must preserve any instructional comments that convey required constraints or important explanations

rule: Keep types-* stub packages excluded from automated dependency bumps; their version must be pinned to match the installed version of the upstream runtime dependency they type.
trigger: A renovate/dependabot config adds or removes a types-* entry from the ignore/exclude list, or a types-* pin is bumped without a matching bump of its upstream package.
rationale: Stub packages are coupled to a specific upstream release (types-protobuf 6.32.1.x matches protobuf 6.32.0); automated bots do not check that pairing, so maintainers verify it manually every time.

evidence.excerpt: types-* packages are coupled to the corresponding version for their upstream dependency

rule: Guard CI jobs that consume repository secrets so they are skipped, not failed, when the secret is unavailable - notably on pull_request runs from forks.
trigger: A workflow step or job references secrets.* (or validates a token via a validate_*_secret script) without an if: condition on the secret being present or on the event not being a fork pull_request.
rationale: Fork pull requests cannot access repository secrets, so an unguarded secret-validation step turns every external contributor's PR red for a reason unrelated to their change.

evidence.excerpt: Skip the activation job when COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN isn't available (e.g., pull_request runs from forks)

rule: Write all code comments, docstrings and identifiers in English; non-English comments must be translated before merge.
trigger: An added line inside homeassistant/components/ contains a comment or docstring with non-ASCII, non-English text (e.g. CJK characters).
rationale: The codebase is maintained by an international contributor base and reviewed in English; comments in another language are unreadable to most maintainers of the integration.

evidence.excerpt: Remove Chinese comment - only English comments should be used in the codebase

rule: Every rule status in an integration's quality_scale.yaml must reflect what the code actually implements; do not leave a rule as todo when the corresponding implementation is already present.
trigger: A quality_scale.yaml adds or keeps a rule marked todo/exempt while the integration source already contains the implementation for that rule (e.g. config-entry-unloading: todo alongside async_unload_entry in __init__.py).
rationale: The quality scale file is the authoritative record of an integration's tier; a stale todo understates the integration's level and hides which rules still need work.

evidence.excerpt: Mark config-entry-unloading as done (not todo) since the integration implements async_unload_entry

rule: Normalize MAC addresses with homeassistant.helpers.device_registry.format_mac before using them as a config entry unique ID or device identifier; never hand-roll uppercasing/colon insertion.
trigger: A config flow or entity builds a MAC string via .upper(), .lower(), string slicing or ":".join(...) and passes it to async_set_unique_id or device identifiers.
rationale: Manual normalization assumes a particular length and separator format from the discovery source; the shared helper is what the rest of the codebase uses, so hand-rolled variants produce unique IDs that do not match other flows.

evidence.excerpt: Using the shared helper (format_mac) would better match patterns used across the codebase

rule: A service handler must only index call.data with keys declared in that specific service's voluptuous schema; for optional or per-service fields use call.data.get() and handle the missing case.
trigger: A shared service handler branches on an attribute constant and reads call.data[ATTR_X] where ATTR_X is not part of the schema registered for the service being executed.
rationale: Services registered with different schemas share one handler, so indexing a key another service defines raises KeyError at call time for users of the service that omits the field.

evidence.excerpt: only read a value from call.data for services that actually define that field

rule: Authentication failures that start a reauth flow must surface a distinct user-facing message stating that reauthentication is required, and must not interpolate the raw exception text into it.
trigger: An except clause groups an authentication error with connection/transport errors into one HomeAssistantError whose message is generic or embeds f"...{err}".
rationale: The user-visible message is the only cue that credentials need re-entering; collapsing it into the generic connection wording hides the required action, and raw exception text is too technical for the frontend.

evidence.excerpt: consider returning an error message that indicates reauthentication is required

rule: Gate conditional entity creation on the capability flag or coordinator data key that actually supplies the entity's value, not on an unrelated module/feature flag.
trigger: An entity is appended inside an if that tests a capability key different from the datapoint key the entity description reads (e.g. entity keyed on hidro.* created only when main.hasCL is set).
rationale: Mismatched gating silently prevents an entity from ever being created on hardware that does provide the datapoint, and there is no error to trace it back to.

evidence.excerpt: Gate this on the correct capability (e.g., hydrolysis presence flag)

rule: When the user step and the reauth step of a config flow perform the same validation, share one implementation and branch on the flow type at the end rather than duplicating the connect/validate block.
trigger: config_flow.py contains async_step_reauth_confirm whose try/except validation body duplicates async_step_user, differing only in the final async_create_entry vs async_update_reload_and_abort.
rationale: Duplicated flow bodies drift apart as error handling changes; existing integrations such as airgradient already model the merged form reviewers ask new integrations to follow.

evidence.excerpt: as you user flow and reauth flow are very similar, you could consider merging them

rule: A coordinator's _async_update_data must not issue one sequential API request per device; use the library's batch endpoint, or at minimum asyncio.gather, so the polling interval does not multiply request volume by device count.
trigger: _async_update_data contains a for-loop over devices with an awaited per-device API call inside it, following an initial list/devices call.
rationale: With a short update interval an N+1 fan-out scales request volume with the user's device count (10 devices = 11 requests/minute) and can trip cloud rate limits for everyone using the integration.

evidence.excerpt: This loop makes one API call per device on every update cycle (N+1 pattern)

rule: Keep device- and API-specific data marshalling (timestamp formatting, parameter string construction) in the upstream vendor library rather than in the integration's coordinator.
trigger: A coordinator or entity module defines helpers that format datetimes or build vendor-specific request parameter strings before passing them to the library client.
rationale: Formatting rules belong to the device's API contract; keeping them in the library keeps the integration thin and means format changes are fixed once upstream instead of in core.

evidence.excerpt: it would be very cool if the library handles the datetime -> string part

rule: Adding an entity platform module, or a new entity description to an existing platform's descriptions tuple, requires accompanying tests covering entity creation and state - with snapshot assertions for entity attributes.
trigger: A diff adds homeassistant/components/<domain>/<platform>.py or appends an EntityDescription with a new key/device_class, without a matching added or extended tests/components/<domain>/test_<platform>.py.
rationale: Untested platforms and device-class mappings regress silently during setup or state handling; integrations here are expected to have per-platform tests with snapshots the way their init and config-flow modules already do.

evidence.excerpt: the sensor platform should similarly have tests covering entity creation, state values, and snapshot assertions
Add tests that cover creation and state reporting for the new open window binary sensor

rule: Key entity caches and lookup dictionaries by a stable unique identifier (the entity's unique_id), never by its display name.
trigger: A module stores entities in a dict keyed by a human-readable name variable (sensor_name, friendly name, topic label) and later checks `if key not in store` to decide between creating and updating.
rationale: Display names are not globally unique - two devices or topics can both produce "Barometer" - so a name-keyed store lets one sensor overwrite another or receive another's updates.

evidence.excerpt: Key the store by a stable unique identifier (unique_id) instead of the display name

rule: User-facing strings in strings.json must follow Home Assistant string style: spell out "for example" instead of "e.g.", avoid slash constructions such as "Folder/Prefix", and wrap literal example values in backticks rather than quotes.
trigger: An added or changed value in strings.json (name, description, data_description) contains a slash-joined noun pair, "e.g.", or an example value in single/double quotes.
rationale: These strings are shown in the config flow UI and are translated downstream; the project's string style guidance keeps them readable and consistently translatable across integrations.

evidence.excerpt: avoid the slash and use backticks for the example value

rule: Log per-item skip or parse failures at debug level; reserve _LOGGER.warning for conditions the user can act on and that cannot repeat once per listed item.
trigger: A _LOGGER.warning call sits inside a loop over remote objects/files in an except branch that merely skips the item.
rationale: A bucket or listing can contain many unrelated items, so a per-item warning floods the log for a condition the user cannot fix; diagnostics stay available at debug level.

evidence.excerpt: Logging a warning per skipped metadata file can become noisy

rule: A failing backup agent must fail only itself: an exception raised by one backup platform must not abort the overall backup or the other platforms, and the platform API contract is documented rather than defensively re-validated.
trigger: Changes to the backup agent/platform API (agent.py, manager.py) that propagate a single agent's exception into the shared backup flow, or add per-call validation of platform-supplied callbacks.
rationale: Integrations can always contain bugs; the manager's job is isolation of the offending platform, and the documented platform API is the contract rather than runtime checks in core.

evidence.excerpt: We should just make sure that it's only that backup platform that will fail

rule: Do not silence an untyped third-party return value with a broad `# type: ignore`; cast the value explicitly (e.g. int(...)) or add typing for the library function.
trigger: A return statement or assignment gains a `# type: ignore[no-any-return]` (or similar blanket ignore) around a call into an untyped external dependency.
rationale: The ignore comment disables checking for the whole statement, so later type errors on that line go unreported; an explicit cast keeps the annotation meaningful.

evidence.excerpt: Replace the broad type-ignore on the return statement with an explicit int cast

rule: An entity lifecycle override must call the matching base-class hook (async_will_remove_from_hass calls super().async_will_remove_from_hass()); never satisfy the home-assistant-missing-super-call check by calling a different hook or by disabling it.
trigger: An overridden async_added_to_hass / async_will_remove_from_hass calls a super() method with a different name, or adds `# pylint: disable-next=home-assistant-missing-super-call`.
rationale: The custom pylint check exists because skipping or crossing lifecycle hooks leaves base-class subscriptions and cleanup in an inconsistent state; disabling it hides exactly the bug it detects.

evidence.excerpt: Call the correct removal hook on the base class (async_will_remove_from_hass)
